sections.title: What is Union-Find (DSU)?
sections.content:
Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union, DSU) tracks which elements belong to the same connected component and can merge two components. Two operations: `find(x)` returns the root representative of x's component; `union(x, y)` merges the components of x and y.

This powers Kruskal's MST, undirected cycle detection, dynamic connectivity (BFS/DFS can't efficiently handle graphs where edges are added incrementally), and equivalence class problems like 'accounts merge'.

Naive implementation (follow parent pointers to root) degrades to O(n) per operation. Two optimizations bring this to effectively O(1) amortized:

**Path compression**: during `find(x)`, set every node on the path directly to the root. Future finds skip to root in O(1).

**Union by rank/size**: attach the smaller tree under the larger one. Prevents chains from forming.

With both optimizations, operations run in O(α(n)) where α is the inverse Ackermann function — effectively O(1) for all practical n. The implementation is ~20 lines.

sections.title: When to Use This
sections.content: Use Union-Find for dynamic connectivity — edges added incrementally and you need fast 'are these two nodes connected' queries. Also for undirected cycle detection and Kruskal's MST. If the graph is static and you only need components once, BFS/DFS is simpler.
signals: is there a path between X and Y

sections.title: Path Compression, Union by Rank, and Cycle Detection
sections.content:
## Core Structure

```
parent[i] = i  // each node starts as its own root
rank[i] = 0    // approximate tree height
```

## find(x) — Path Compression

```
find(x):
  if parent[x] !== x:
    parent[x] = find(parent[x])  // flatten to root
  return parent[x]
```

After compression, future finds on any node in this path go directly to root.

## union(x, y) — Union by Rank

Find roots rx and ry. If same root, already connected (adding edge = cycle). Otherwise attach smaller rank under larger:
```
if rank[rx] < rank[ry]: parent[rx]=ry
else if rank[rx] > rank[ry]: parent[ry]=rx
else: parent[ry]=rx; rank[rx]++  // only increment on equal-rank merge
```

## Cycle Detection — Undirected

Process edges one by one. Before adding (u,v): if `find(u) === find(v)`, they're already connected — adding this edge creates a cycle. Otherwise `union(u, v)`.

## Connected Components Count

Initialize `components = n`. Each successful union decrements by 1. At any point, `components` gives the current count.

## Equivalence Classes

In accounts merge: union accounts sharing an email. After all unions, group accounts by root representative.

sections.title: Core Template
sections.explanation: DSU with path compression and union by rank. components count maintained automatically. union returning false directly signals a cycle for undirected graphs.

items.name: Weighted DSU
items.description: Augment each node with a weight relative to its parent. During path compression accumulate weights. Used when tracking 'distance' or 'ratio' between connected nodes, not just connectivity.
items.example_problem: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column

items.name: Virtual Nodes in DSU
items.description: For entities of different types (rows and columns, email accounts), create virtual nodes for groups. Union real nodes with their virtual group node instead of directly with each other.

items.name: Redundant Edge Detection
items.description: Add edges one by one. The first edge where union returns false (both endpoints already share a root) is the redundant edge creating a cycle.

sections.title: Complexity
sections.explanation: With path compression and union by rank, each operation runs in O(α(n)) amortized where α is the inverse Ackermann function — at most 5 for any realistic n. Without path compression: O(log n) with union by rank, O(n) without either. Space is O(n) for parent and rank arrays.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Checking parent[x]===parent[y] instead of find(x)===find(y) for connectivity — two nodes can be in the same component with different immediate parents. Always use find which follows to the root.
Forgetting path compression makes parent[x] not necessarily the root — always call find(x) recursively, never read parent[x] directly as the representative.
Incrementing rank on every union instead of only on equal-rank merges — overstates tree height and degrades the union-by-rank guarantee.
Using DSU for directed graphs — DSU tracks undirected connectivity only. 'A can reach B but B cannot reach A' is not captured by DSU.
In accounts merge style problems: attempting to union by email string directly — DSU operates on integer indices. Map email → account index first.
